title: Developer Experience: SDK Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Ops, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes standards and operating procedures for the Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation set that supports Redwood Inference SDKs, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical fixes we use in support. It is intended for DevEx engineers, technical writers, on-call engineers, and solutions engineers who author or maintain user-facing examples.

Goals
- Provide consistent, copy-and-pasteable SDK examples that work with the current Redwood API and SDKs.
- Maintain a small set of curated quickstarts & templates for common patterns (chat, embeddings, streaming, fine-tuning proxies).
- Keep the docs site publishing workflow simple and auditable.
- Track top support issues and publish canonical fixes that can be included in quickstarts and troubleshooting pages.

Scope
- SDKs: official JS/TS and Python SDKs, plus community-supported SDK snippets.
- Quickstarts & templates: 1) Chat web demo, 2) Background jobs (batch embeddings), 3) Lambda-style serverless inference proxy, 4) Canary deploy example.
- API examples: text generation, chat + function calling, embeddings, reranking, streaming.
- Docs operations: review checklist, CI validation, release tagging, rollback.
- Support issues: tracked canonical fixes and reproducible tests.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner_team: engineering (DevEx team).
- Document owner: Asha Patel (DevEx lead).
- On-call owner for example regressions: eng-developer-experience oncall rotation.

Standards for SDK Guides and Examples
1) Always keep examples minimal and runnable. Prefer complete copy-paste examples over fragments.
2) Use the latest stable SDK versions in examples. Include a changelog note at top when we intentionally pin older versions.
3) Authentication: show both environment variable and explicit token examples.
4) Include a short explanation of the expected output and common failure modes.
5) Add comment blocks with links to related docs and the API reference.
6) Test every example in CI (see Docs CI section below).

Example: Minimal Python text generation\n```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-medium-2", prompt="Write a short haiku about coffee.")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates: Canonical Set
- Chat web demo (React + streaming): base template that wires SDK streaming to UI tokens + reconnection logic.
- Batch embeddings pipeline (Airflow example): demonstrates chunking, concurrency, and caching best practices.
- Serverless inference proxy (AWS Lambda / GCP Cloud Run): shows request throttling, cold-start mitigation, and token budgeting.
- Canary deploy example: config for model rollouts using route weights and automatic fallback.

Each quickstart must include:
- README with purpose and pre-reqs.
- Config file (YAML) with example values.
- Automated smoke test that runs in our CI.

Docs site operating procedures (publish workflow)
1) Authoring and PRs
   - Create a branch named `docs/<short-desc>` and open a doc PR against the `main` docs repo.
   - Assign at least one reviewer from the DevEx team and one owner of the affected SDK (labels: `devex`, `sdk-js` or `sdk-py`).
   - In the PR description include: short summary, affected pages, example artifacts (screenshots/recording), and the smoke-test command.
2) Review checklist (must be green before merge)
   - Examples run locally with `make smoke-test` and CI passes.
   - API versions and SDK versions updated if needed.
   - Accessibility: example UI pages meet basic accessibility checks (alt text, keyboard navigation).
   - Security review if doc shows customer data, credentials handling, or private deploy steps.
3) CI validation steps
   - Linting (markdown style and prose).
   - Link checker (fail on broken internal links).
   - Live-run smoke tests for code examples (Python/Node).
   - Example output snapshot comparison (for non-deterministic outputs, we allow regex matches).
4) Release and tagging
   - Docs merged to `main` are auto-deployed to staging.
   - After a full smoke-test pass on staging, a Release Engineer tags the PR with `release/docs` to promote to production.
   - Emergency rollbacks: revert the doc PR and re-run site deploy; notify #devex-docs and #sre.

Template: Docs PR description (checklist)
1. Short summary of change
2. Files changed list
3. Smoke test command and result
4. Reviewers assigned
5. Label(s) added

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes
We maintain a short table of the most-frequent developer-facing support issues and the canonical fixes that should be surfaced in docs and quickstarts. Include owner and mitigation guidance.

| Issue ID | Symptom | Root cause (common) | Canonical fix | Workaround / Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DX-101 | SDK auth errors: 401 during local dev | Missing/expired API key, or env var not loaded | Update quickstart to show `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` and `client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))` example. Add token-check helper. | Show command to validate token: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account` | DevEx - Asha P. |
| DX-117 | Streaming disconnects / truncated responses | Incomplete reconnect/backoff logic in UI or incorrect 'stream' flag | Add reconnect + resume logic in React example; ensure `stream: true` set on request. | Use non-streamed fallback in server-side components for short term | Frontend DevEx - Leo C. |
| DX-124 | High latency on batch embeddings | Improper batching size / single-threaded uploader | Update Airflow example to use chunking (batch_size=256 tokens) and concurrency=8, show caching layer (Redis) for re-used texts. | Lower concurrency or use Dedicated capacity for large jobs | SRE - Morgan R. |
| DX-133 | Rate limit 429 when running many parallel requests | No client-side rate limiter / unbounded retry storm | Add client library rate-limiter usage and exponential backoff with jitter example. | Queue requests with local bucket; reduce concurrency | DevEx - Priya S. |

(Note: above table is canonical guidance; each row should map to a short troubleshooting page with copyable commands.)

Canonical Fix Example: Rate limiter (NodeJS snippet)
```js
const limiter = new TokenBucket({capacity: 50, refillRate: 5});
async function callApi(req) {
  await limiter.removeToken();
  return await client.generate({model: 'redwood-medium-2', prompt: req.prompt});
}
```

Testing and CI requirements for examples
- Every code example must have a smoke test under `devex/examples/smoke-tests/` that can run in CI without paid API access (use recorded fixtures or a lightweight local mocking server).
- For examples that require live API keys (integration tests), CI should run them only on protected branches and require a `DOCS_LIVE_TESTS=true` flag and approved owner.

Maintenance cadence and ownership
- Quarterly review: DevEx team performs a doc sweep to validate SDK examples after each SDK minor release.
- Incident-linked updates: any support incident that yields a reproducible fix must result in a docs update within 5 business days.
- Deprecation: when an API or SDK is deprecated, add a clear deprecation banner to all affected docs and plan a migration guide.

Appendix: Useful commands and checklists
- Local smoke test: `make smoke-test-examples`
- Run single example: `python examples/text_gen/smoke_test.py` or `node examples/chat/smoke_test.js`
- Lint docs: `npm run docs:lint`
- Verify links: `npm run docs:link-check`

Related resources
- DevEx SDK repository: git@github.com:redwood-inference/devex-sdks.git
- Docs site runbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-operating-procedures-2026

If you have suggestions for additional quickstarts or canonical fixes, open a PR against the `devex-docs` repo and tag `@devex-leads`.
